title: introduce-chorus-attn-kernel-with-opcache-and-lane-reservation-scheduler
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: reduce tail latency and per-token GPU cost for mixed short/long chat workloads by introducing a new attention kernel (Chorus) that combines a banded tiled attention path with an in-GPU opcache for hot KV slices, and a lane-reservation scheduler to improve continuous batching locality. This PR implements the Chorus kernel, a lightweight opcache layer for KV hot slices (opcache), and an adaptive lane-reservation scheduler that maintains low SLO violations under bursty traffic. The changeset includes CUDA kernel code, scheduler integration, e2e perf harness updates, and unit/integration tests. Checklist: - [x] Implement Chorus attention kernel with fused rotary/op fusion path - [x] Add opcache for KV hot-slices with fallback to main KV store - [x] Integrate lane-reservation scheduler with continuous batcher - [x] Add synthetic and replay perf tests and baseline comparisons - [x] Add runtime flags and telemetry (metrics/traces) - [x] Add docs snippet for operator flags and rollout plan High-level approach: Chorus kernel implements a narrow-band tiled attention path for sequence windows up to 2048 tokens with a fused rotary multiplication and qkv-permute fusion to reduce memory traffic. The kernel supports an opcache region stored in GPU memory (configurable size) for recently-accessed KV slices; cache lookup is O(1) with an LRU-ish eviction tuned for prefix reuse patterns seen in chat workloads. Scheduler changes allow lane reservations: requests are mapped to ephemeral lanes keyed by model+session so that KV-cache hits are preserved across contiguous requests; the lane-reservation logic holds a lane for short periods (configurable 10-200ms) before releasing it, allowing continuous batching to coalesce while preserving latency SLOs. Rollout plan: staged canary on dedicated pool -> 10% hosted -> 50% hosted -> full by config. Observability: added metrics redwood.attn.chorus.opcache.hit_ratio, redwood.attn.chorus.evictions, redwood.scheduler.lane_reservations.active, per-route tail latency percentiles. Backwards compatibility: kernel registers as an alternate implementation selected by runtime policy. If opcache is disabled or memory constraints hit, runtime falls back to the existing flashbridge-attn path. Performance summary (internal perf harness, T4-like instance): - 95th latency improved by 18-28% for mixed short/long chat trace - per-token GPU cycles decreased by ~12% on average for warm sessions - throughput for long-context batch steady-state up by ~6% Commits: - Implement chorus kernel initial prototype and microbench harness - Add opcache allocator and eviction policy - Integrate lane reservation into continuous batcher and routing - Perf harness updates and new replay traces - Tests and docs, flag gating, unit tests - Fix CI failures (memory fence ordering, thread-safety) Merge notes: this was rolled as a squash merge after CI perf checks and a small canary run.

release_notes: Introduce Chorus attention kernel: a banded tiled attention implementation with fused rotary and an in-GPU opcache for hot KV slices. Adds lane-reservation scheduling to improve continuous batching locality. Performance: improved 95p latency for mixed chat workloads and reduced per-token GPU cycles for warm sessions. Rollout behind runtime flags. No breaking changes.
